MINI HANABI. You and two teammates share one score. Build the red (R) and blue (B) piles in order 1, then 2, then 3. Each built card earns one team point. Completing BOTH piles within six turns earns an additional six-point completion bonus: 12 points total. A discard or review still costs a turn, leaving fewer turns to build. Each nine-card challenge deal contains all six colour/rank combinations plus three duplicates, arranged into three hands of three. Colours, teammate seats and your slot order vary between deals. There are no draws. You see your teammates' cards; your own cards are hidden. Before each turn a teammate gives you a free colour or rank clue. Every matching slot is marked, and earlier marks remain with their cards. On your turn choose exactly one action: play one of your own cards with [play: N], give a teammate a clue with [clue: player P, R] or [clue: player P, 1], or request a review with [review: 0]. Slots are numbered from 1, left to right. A played card scores only if it is next for its colour; otherwise it is discarded. After any card is played, remaining cards shift left. For a clue, choose player 1 or 2 and write one colour (R or B) or rank (1, 2 or 3) present in their hand. The clue must contain only that information. It costs one of your three clue tokens. The recipient immediately plays their leftmost matching card. Teammates do not take separate play turns. A review uses your turn to check your clue marks; it must not reveal unmarked card information. The game ends after six turns, when all hands are empty, or when both piles reach 3. Clue letters may be upper or lower case; letter case has no card meaning. [appeal: last] asks a clerk to reconsider your last discarded card; correctly resolved discards are final.
